# Najmul Hasan

> Najmul Hasan is a researcher whose interests center on language models and AI alignment. He is particularly interested in the design and training of language models, including how training choices shape their capabilities and behavior, and in developing models that are more capable, reliable, and aligned. He holds a B.S. in Computer Science with minors in Mathematics and Physics from the University of North Carolina at Pembroke, where he worked with Dr. Prashanth BusiReddyGari and Dr. Shaohu Zhang. He was an AI Safety Research Fellow at Algoverse. He is currently participating in MIT AI Alignment's AI Safety Fundamentals program and has completed BlueDot Impact's Technical AI Safety course.

## Research Papers

- [GRPO Does Not Close the Multi-Agent Coordination Gap](https://najmulhasan-code.github.io/research/grpo-coordination): A study of whether GRPO fine-tuning can close the coordination gap between Qwen3-14B and stronger language models on a Dining Philosophers benchmark. Across 630 episodes, the saved GRPO checkpoint produced no statistically significant improvement over the base model and exposed limitations in reward shaping and checkpoint selection. arXiv preprint, Jun 2026. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07845) | [Code](https://github.com/najmulhasan-code/dpmarl)

- [CRC-Screen: Certified DNA-Synthesis Hazard Screening Under Taxonomic Shift](https://najmulhasan-code.github.io/research/crc-screen): A conformal-risk-control screener for DNA-synthesis biosecurity that fuses k-mer Jaccard similarity, a five-LLM judge panel, and embedding-centroid cosine similarity into a calibrated aggregator with a certified false-negative-rate bound; achieves 0% test miss rate across leave-one-taxonomic-family-out folds on UniProt KW-0800 toxins. arXiv preprint, Apr 2026. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00074) | [Code](https://github.com/najmulhasan-code/crc-screen)

- [Honeypot Protocol](https://najmulhasan-code.github.io/research/honeypot-protocol): Trusted monitoring, the standard defense in AI control, is vulnerable to adaptive attacks, collusion, and strategic attack selection. The honeypot protocol tests context-dependent behavior in AI systems by varying system prompts across evaluation, deployment, and no-monitoring conditions. AI Control Hackathon by Apart Research, 2026. [Paper](https://apartresearch.com/project/honeypot-protocol-hmsb) | [Code](https://github.com/najmulhasan-code/honeypot-protocol)

- [DPBench: Large Language Models Struggle with Simultaneous Coordination](https://najmulhasan-code.github.io/research/dpbench): A benchmark based on the Dining Philosophers problem showing LLMs fail at simultaneous coordination with deadlock rates exceeding 95%. Communication alone does not resolve coordination failures. arXiv preprint, Feb 2026. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13255) | [Code](https://github.com/najmulhasan-code/dpbench)

- [Benchmarking Large Language Models for Zero-shot and Few-shot Phishing URL Detection](https://najmulhasan-code.github.io/research/phishing-url-detection): Comprehensive benchmark of LLMs under zero-shot and few-shot prompting for phishing URL detection; few-shot prompting with 6 examples raised best model accuracy from 89% to 94%. LAW Workshop at NeurIPS 2025. [Paper](https://openreview.net/forum?id=COmhlLFVk9) | [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02641)

- [Time-Complexity Characterization of the NIST Lightweight Cryptography Finalists](https://najmulhasan-code.github.io/research/nist-crypto): Symbolic model decomposing NIST lightweight cryptography finalists into initialization, data-processing, and finalization phases for formal time-complexity derivation. IEEE CCWC 2026. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/CCWC67433.2026.11393752) | [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05641)

- [Phishing Email Detection Using Large Language Models](https://najmulhasan-code.github.io/research/phishing-email-detection): LLM-PEA framework evaluating three frontier LLMs against adversarial, prompt injection, and cross-lingual phishing attacks across 4,000+ email samples; revealed up to 904% false positive rate increase in non-English settings. arXiv preprint, Dec 2025. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10104)
